meta.title: Inventory of the library pathways page
meta.how_to_read: Each entry is one item a reader can reach. Each test says how to find it again in a page. Tests are hard unless "soft" is set. where: base = the page as it opens; open = after every disclosure is opened; any = either, or after clicking through. A probe clicks or sets controls, then checks the page.

conventions.text: The page inlines its model as one <script type="application/json"> holding the keys map, params, lims, cases and text (the shapes in the data files; cases may be packed). The picture is the model: the check reads the counts from here.
conventions.tested: data entries (hard on the current page)

conventions.text: Every drawn state carries data-state="<state id>" and every drawn branch carries data-branch="<branch id>".
The control that opens a limitation carries data-lim="LIM-nn"; the control that opens a case carries data-case="<case id>"; each slider row carries data-param="<unknown id>".
conventions.tested: soft; the case probes also fall back to the selectors of the current page

conventions.text: Every reveal is a <details> element or a control with aria-expanded. Every choice that stays pressed carries aria-pressed. Every click-to-select mark is a button or has role="button". The check opens everything by these.
conventions.tested: soft, through what the check can open

conventions.text: A mark that has no printed number (a plotted point, a spread row, a square cell) carries its exact value: data-chart + data-period + data-v on each ratio point; data-spread + data-p5/p25/p50/p75/p95 on each spread row; data-cell="i,j" + data-v on each square cell.

Numbers keep the rounding they have now, so that a check can find them: ratios 2 decimals (1 decimal from 10), costs 1 decimal (0 from 100), shares and weights 1 decimal with a percent sign, correlations signed with 2 decimals.
conventions.tested: hard (the check searches the formatted text)

conventions.text: A step judgment shows its status as a word (works, strains, breaks, not specified, not reached) in text beside its note, or as an accessible name on a mark inside the same element.
A control that is renamed in the redesign is listed in an aliases file: { "<test id>": "<new text>" } or an array of accepted texts. The check reads it with --aliases and reports every alias it used.
The redesign may drop interaction hints that describe the old layout ("Tap a bar…", "The map scrolls sideways"). These tests are marked soft with a reason. Everything else is a hard test.

Where real cases went the other way
Same mistake, new session: Helper windows in the same folder receive CLAUDE.md and the memory index at transcript line 6. They lack only what the session learned since the last memory write.
Silent defect found later: Fresh windows found every defect: the adversarial audit, the red team, the adversarial re-read, the root reviews. Emptiness was the asset here.
Building new beside old: The copies were made in long main sessions (835 and 831 calls). Helper windows were reviewers, and they caught defects.
Races and flaky failures: The review that refuted the wrong hypothesis was a fresh helper window told to refute. Its empty window was not anchored by the main session's guess.
Research and design cases: Fresh Sonnet gatherers with a pointed brief found the withdrawal and summarised a 972-line design accurately.
Across projects: The helper windows carried the shell rule in their briefs. The windows lacking cross-project knowledge were the long-lived Fable sessions.
Existing notes over time: MEMORY.md and CLAUDE.md sit at line 6 or 7 of every helper window checked (three sessions). Only index lines arrive; a note's body needs a read or a brief.

Silent defect found later: No case climbed. Nothing failed visibly, so the rung costs never arose.
Building new beside old: No rung was climbed in any case. Defects were found after merge by reviews, audits, test runs or a drill.
Outside vendor causes: The reasoning was cheap. The cost was the outside round trip (a cloud build, a deploy, a machine rebuild), and no rung changes that.
Research and design cases: No case climbed the ladder in order. The cost was review rounds at one tier plus owner turns.
Across projects: No case climbed. Every fix was cheap once known; the cost was not knowing.
The ladder in real life: One rung was paid, Fable for about a minute. The cost was two check runs, not a climb.

entries.label: R1 reinforcing: Bad entries bring more bad entries

tests.s: Bad entries bring more bad entries

More bad entries raise the bad share a lookup returns. More wrong entries reach the cheap attempt and spoil work. More work climbs to Opus or Fable. More solves and escapes get written, some of them bad.

entries.label: R2 reinforcing: More entries, more look-alikes

tests.s: Every entry, good or bad, raises the chance a look-alike is found. Accepted look-alikes spoil work. More work climbs the ladder, and more entries get written.

entries.label: B1 balancing: Good entries thin their own supply

tests.s: Good entries thin their own supply
More good entries fill the library. The cheap model is right more often with one in hand. Less work climbs to Opus or Fable, so fewer entries are written.

entries.label: B2 balancing: Good entries go stale

tests.s: Each period a share of good entries goes stale and moves to the bad stock. The more good entries, the more go stale.

entries.label: R3 reinforcing: More caught at the gate, more climbs, more right strong solves written, more good entries

tests.s: More caught at the gate, more climbs, more right strong solves written, more good entries
Good entries → Checks promoted into the shared tests → The gate catches the wrong output → Share of work that climbs to Opus or Fable → Good entries written per piece of work → Good entries.

entries.label: R4 reinforcing: Fewer strong-tier escapes pass, fewer bad entries written, a smaller bad share

tests.s: Fewer strong-tier escapes pass, fewer bad entries written, a smaller bad share

Good entries → Checks promoted into the shared tests → The gate catches the wrong Opus output → Bad entries written after a strong-tier escape, per piece of work → Bad entries (wrong or stale) → Share of stored entries that are bad.

entries.label: The groups are a judgment

parts: Each library unknown was placed in one group by hand. Promoted checks sit with entry quality, though they need no lookup. The calls an entry saves sit with entry quality too. Look-alikes and staleness could count as properties of the work, beside what comes back. Moving any of these changes some corners. Some move toward the library and some away from it. entries.label: One size of work, and no time

tests.s: One size of work, and no time

parts: Every piece of work is about ten cheap calls. Real work varies far more in size. Tests at the gate cost nothing. Waiting and the owner's attention are left out.

entries.label: Pieces of work are independent

parts: A piece's kind, its need, what the library holds and any look-alike are combined by multiplying chances. Real work clusters. A hard problem may also be the one the library lacks.

entries.label: Averages, not one library

parts: The stocks change by their expected amounts each period. A real library has one history, with luck in it. Nothing written during a period helps that same period.

entries.label: Entries are all-or-nothing

parts: A good entry is good wherever it applies, and a bad one bad. Partly right shows up only as the 'some parts' result.

entries.label: One pool of entries

parts: Projects are not separated. Facts that differ between projects act only through the look-alike and wrong-entry chances.

parts: A wrong entry does not follow the work up the ladder. A good entry does not help the cheap retry or Opus either. Only a promoted check acts later, at the gate.

entries.label: Piece of work

strings: One fix-sized task of about ten cheap calls. A result is made and checked.

tests.s: One fix-sized task of about ten cheap calls. A result is made and checked.

entries.label: Cheap model, Opus and Fable

strings: The cheap model is Sonnet. Opus is the next model up, at a higher price. Fable is the top one.

tests.s: The cheap model is Sonnet. Opus is the next model up, at a higher price. Fable is the top one.

entries.label: Visible or latent

strings: Visible: something signals a problem, such as an error or a failing check. Latent: nothing signals that a choice matters.

tests.s: Visible: something signals a problem, such as an error or a failing check. Latent: nothing signals that a choice matters.

entries.label: Entry

strings: One stored conclusion in the library.

tests.s: One stored conclusion in the library.

entries.label: Lookup

strings: A search of the library for entries that fit the work in hand.

tests.s: A search of the library for entries that fit the work in hand.

entries.label: Look-alike

strings: A stored entry that looks like a match but has a different cause.

tests.s: A stored entry that looks like a match but has a different cause.

entries.label: Several parts

strings: Work that needs two or more entries. A lookup may find all the parts, or only some parts.

tests.s: Work that needs two or more entries. A lookup may find all the parts, or only some parts.

entries.label: Screen

strings: The test of whether a found entry applies, before the cheap model uses it.

tests.s: The test of whether a found entry applies, before the cheap model uses it.

entries.label: Mechanical check

strings: A check an entry carries that decides by itself whether the entry applies. No model judges it.

tests.s: A check an entry carries that decides by itself whether the entry applies. No model judges it.

entries.label: Window

strings: The text a model has in front of it while it works.

tests.s: The text a model has in front of it while it works.

entries.label: Stale

strings: A good entry goes stale when what it rests on changes. It then counts as a bad entry.

tests.s: A good entry goes stale when what it rests on changes. It then counts as a bad entry.

entries.label: Capture

strings: Writing a strong model's solve back into the library as an entry.

tests.s: Writing a strong model's solve back into the library as an entry.

entries.label: Ceiling

strings: The most of the work that entries could cover in the long run, beyond today's notes.

tests.s: The most of the work that entries could cover in the long run, beyond today's notes.

entries.label: Gate

strings: Whatever decides a result is right: tests, and sometimes a review by Opus.

tests.s: Whatever decides a result is right: tests, and sometimes a review by Opus.

entries.label: Escape

strings: A wrong result that passes the gate. It may be found later, or never.

tests.s: A wrong result that passes the gate. It may be found later, or never.

entries.label: Ladder

strings: What happens after a caught failure: one cheap retry, then Opus, then Fable.

tests.s: What happens after a caught failure: one cheap retry, then Opus, then Fable.

entries.label: Handoff

strings: Handing a piece of work up to Opus. It has a small cost of its own.

tests.s: Handing a piece of work up to Opus. It has a small cost of its own.

entries.label: Promoted check

strings: An entry's mechanical check that also runs in the shared tests. It acts at the gate with no lookup.

tests.s: An entry's mechanical check that also runs in the shared tests. It acts at the gate with no lookup.

entries.label: Cost

strings: Counted in cheap-call equivalents. One cheap-model call costs one. An Opus call costs the Opus price ratio.

tests.s: Counted in cheap-call equivalents. One cheap-model call costs one. An Opus call costs the Opus price ratio.

entries.label: Wrong rate

strings: The share of pieces of work that do not end accepted and right.

tests.s: The share of pieces of work that do not end accepted and right.

entries.label: Ratio

strings: The library's figure divided by the other way's figure. Below one, the library's figure is lower.

tests.s: The library's figure divided by the other way's figure. Below one, the library's figure is lower.

entries.label: Middle value

strings: The value an unknown starts at, inside its range.

tests.s: The value an unknown starts at, inside its range.

entries.label: Library unknown

strings: An unknown that exists only because of the library. Each has a poor end and a good end.

tests.s: An unknown that exists only because of the library. Each has a poor end and a good end.

entries.label: Good end

strings: The end of a range where the design works as intended. The poor end is the other one.

tests.s: The end of a range where the design works as intended. The poor end is the other one.

entries.label: Comes back

strings: How much of the work comes back, so an entry could exist for it. A property of the work.

tests.s: How much of the work comes back, so an entry could exist for it. A property of the work.

entries.label: Reach

strings: Whether an entry gets to the cheap model: written, looked up, found and in the window.

tests.s: Whether an entry gets to the cheap model: written, looked up, found and in the window.

entries.label: Entry quality

strings: Whether the entry is right and is used rightly.

tests.s: Whether the entry is right and is used rightly.

entries.label: Running cost

strings: What lookups, screens, carrying and writing cost.

tests.s: What lookups, screens, carrying and writing cost.

entries.label: Corner

strings: Comes back, reach and entry quality, each at its poor or its good end. Everything else stays at its middle value.

tests.s: Comes back, reach and entry quality, each at its poor or its good end. Everything else stays at its middle value.

entries.label: All-good setting

strings: Every library unknown at its good end, running cost included. Every other unknown at its middle value.

tests.s: Every library unknown at its good end, running cost included. Every other unknown at its middle value.

entries.label: Full fall

strings: How far the library's cost and wrong rate fall from the middle values to the all-good setting, averaged.

tests.s: How far the library's cost and wrong rate fall from the middle values to the all-good setting, averaged.

entries.label: Alone

strings: What moving only this gives. Its library unknowns go to their good ends. A share of the full fall.

tests.s: What moving only this gives. Its library unknowns go to their good ends. A share of the full fall.

entries.label: Last

strings: What is lost if only this stays. All else is at its good end. A share of the full fall.

tests.s: What is lost if only this stays. All else is at its good end. A share of the full fall.

entries.label: Middle run

strings: The run in the middle when all runs are sorted. Half the runs fall on each side.

tests.s: The run in the middle when all runs are sorted. Half the runs fall on each side.

entries.label: Tie

strings: How far the library unknowns of one group move together across the runs.

tests.s: How far the library unknowns of one group move together across the runs.

entries.label: Rank correlation

strings: How steadily a result rises (+) or falls (−) as one unknown rises across the runs. One means always; zero means no steady link.

tests.s: How steadily a result rises (+) or falls (−) as one unknown rises across the runs. One means always; zero means no steady link.
